description:
FILED s421 (Fable review of s420): the one companion DECREASE s420 spliced
as "pre-existing" without a cause.  Attributed by a three-way probe.

    $a = *main::foo; $b = $a;
    $a =~ s/^X//;   print ref(\$a), "|", ref(\$b), "|$a\n";
    $a =~ s/^\*//;  print ref(\$a), "|$a\n";
    $_ = *main::qux; tr/a-z/A-Z/; print ref(\$_), "|$_\n";

    perl              GLOB|GLOB|*main::foo   SCALAR|main::foo   SCALAR|*MAIN::QUX
    98159c7 (pre-s419d) REF|REF|GLOB(0x1)    SCALAR|main::foo   SCALAR|*MAIN::QUX
    47e0750 / HEAD      REF|REF|GLOB(0x1)    REF|GLOB(0x1)      SCALAR|GLOB(0X4)

So TWO things, one old and one new:

(a) PRE-EXISTING (all three trees): a glob VALUE copied into a scalar
    (`$a = *main::foo`) is not distinguishable from a glob REF (`\*main::foo`)
    in the box model -- `ref(\$a)` answers REF (perl GLOB) and `"$a"` prints
    `GLOB(0x1)` (perl `*main::foo`).  `box-sv`'s typeglob branch
    ("Blessed typeglob ref: stringify as GLOB(0xADDR) not *PKG::NAME") prints
    EVERY box holding a typeglob as a ref; `stringify-value` on the RAW
    typeglob prints the value spelling `*main::foo` (#316).

(b) s419d (#119/#402, `79702aa`) changed `do-regex-subst` and the tr/// source
    from `(to-string (unbox string-box))` to `(to-string string-box)` so the
    `""` overload and tie FETCH run -- correct for those, but it moved a glob
    value from the value spelling to the ref spelling, so `$a =~ s/^\*//` no
    longer matches and `tr` rewrites `GLOB(0X4)`.  That is op/gv.t's row at
    line 67-69 (50/47 -> 49/48; `docs/perl-suite-run.tsv` carries the splice).
    perl-tests has NO gv.t, so the sweep could not see it; only the op/
    companion leg could, and s419d did not run it (ruled s421: a cl/ coercion
    or stringification change runs op/).

MEASURE FIRST (the cheap discriminating question): how is `\*FOO` represented
vs `*FOO` in a box today -- is the ref a WRAPPED box (box-in-box, the #163
%p-ref-referent machinery) while the value is the bare typeglob in the box?
If they already differ structurally, the fix is one branch in box-sv
(the bare-typeglob case prints the value spelling, the wrapped case the ref
spelling) and `ref(\$a)` follows; then `"$a"` interpolation of a glob value
is fixed too (pre-existing silent wrong).  If they are IDENTICAL in the box,
this is a representation decision (s335 ruled NO ref-kind slot -- re-raise
with this measurement rather than adding one silently), and the interim
answer is the s419d one (consistent ref spelling everywhere; document the
glob-value divergence in not-supported.md with op/gv.t's rows as the cost).

Acceptance: the probe above vs perl; `my $r = \*STDOUT; print "$r"` still
`GLOB(0x...)`; `local *FH; print *FH` still `*main::FH`; op/gv.t back to
>= 50 C_ok; the op/ companion leg.  Guard in Pl/t/overload-01.t (s419d's own
guard file) or the glob test file.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLOSED s424 (2026-08-22, Opus).  Commit on branch
worktree-agent-a5178ca3864cd0e12.

THE MEASUREMENT (the task's discriminating question), first thing:
they DIFFER structurally, and the discriminator ALREADY EXISTS ???
`p-box-is-ref`.  p-backslash sets it on a typeglob wrapper (runtime ~12885),
box-set propagates it (~1721), and **box-nv has read it since #163**: a bare
glob numifies to 0, a glob ref to its address.  Only box-sv and p-ref ignored
it.  So `$g = *foo` printed GLOB(0x1) *while numifying to 0* ??? the #163 rule
("the word and the number agree") broken in place, not a representation gap.
=> fix shape (a).  NOTHING was added to the box: the s335 no-ref-kind-slot
ruling is CONFIRMED by this measurement, not bypassed.

(A second, weaker shape exists: `$pkgvar = \*foo` takes p-scalar-='s literal
reference branch and stores box-in-box, where a lexical stores flat.  Both
resolve through %p-ref-referent; only %p-ref-string had no typeglob-referent
arm, which is why `our $r = \*STDOUT; print "$r"` printed SCALAR(0x???).)

WHAT SHIPPED ??? one rule, normative in docs/ir-spec.md ?S2.5: a typeglob is the
ONE payload whose ref-ness lives on the BOX, not on the object; a RAW typeglob
outside a box is a glob VALUE (stringify-value's convention, #316).
  readers (via the new %p-glob-value-box-p): box-sv, %p-ref-string (its
  MISSING typeglob-referent arm, a closed-set hole that fell through to the
  caller's SCALAR fallback), p-ref (both the payload arm and the referent arm).
  copy paths ??? the half this task did NOT predict, and the readers becoming
  honest is what exposed them: %p-flatten-list (its preserve-list omitted
  typeglobs -> `my $x = shift` on a glob ref degraded to a glob value),
  %p-array-store-scalar, p-aref-unbox-elem.

WHAT NOT TO RETRY: preserving the SOURCE BOX in %p-flatten-list.  It carries
the flag and ALIASES ??? ($g1,$g2) = ($g2,$g1) collapsed to one glob (perl
swaps), and two swapped glob refs collapsed to one address.  The snapshot must
be a FRESH box carrying is-ref.  Guarded, ref-identity-01.t t37-t39.
Also do NOT widen the same rule to STREAMS in this task ??? that is #436.

NUMBERS: gate 155/5631 (5614 + 17 guard rows), failures = the 13 pclxs xs
rows.  Sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18364 -> 18365 (+1: perl-tests/substr.t
374->375, the substr.t:784 `\substr does not coerce its glob arg` row), drops
7 = census.  Companion 12-file op/+io/ leg: op/gv.t 49/48 -> 61/36 and
op/substr.t 376/24 -> 377/23 (both A/B'd on an a2ac578 worktree = 49/48 and
376/24; spliced into perl-suite-run.tsv with the cause), ten files identical.
~60 probe shapes vs perl 5.40.3, also under PCL_OPT=none.  Generation v2-166.

RESIDUE FILED (all A/B-verified pre-existing on the base runtime): #436 (a
lexical filehandle is a raw STREAM: ref($fh) is "" where perl says GLOB ??? the
same family one payload over, deliberately not widened), #437 (\*foo == \*foo
is FALSE: p-make-typeglob mints a fresh struct per mention), #438 (*b =
$pkgvar holding \*foo installs the SCALAR slot).  One more, unfiled because it
is a one-line box-set question rather than a glob one: box-set never CLEARS
is-ref, so `my $n = \*foo; $n = "plain"; ref(\$n)` is REF where perl says
SCALAR (pre-existing; same at the base).

ASKS: docs/opus5-review-requests-s424.md ?S5 ??? the scope of the copy-path half,
the extra type test on p-aref-unbox-elem's hot path, and whether ref() on a
RAW typeglob should keep the old lenient GLOB as a belt.
title: A GLOB VALUE held in a scalar stringifies as GLOB(0x..) on the BOX path (glob value == glob ref in the box model); s419d moved s///+tr/// onto that path -- op/gv.t 50/47 -> 49/48 (REGRESSION, attributed s421)
